idiom_name: module-scoped implementation with #private fields or closure state
implementation_notes: Nothing recompiles a JavaScript consumer when a package's internals change, so the goal is the published shape: export only the API from the module, keep everything else module-local, declare entry points with the package.json exports map so deep paths cannot reach internals, and hold state in #private fields, closures or WeakMaps instead of a reachable property. Where the body must stay genuinely unreachable or swappable, publish a factory that returns an object whose implementation no one can name - the closure captures the real state and only the returned methods touch it. There is no header and no ABI here, so hidden means unexported and unreachable.
pitfalls: export * barrels and published deep paths (pkg/internal/thing) leak implementation by accident, and once a version is published those names are de-facto API; use explicit named exports and the exports map to cut the paths off.

Closure and WeakMap state costs memory and can defeat engine optimizations, while #private fields are faster and unenumerable but per-class and un-mockable - choose based on whether you need a test seam.

Protecting internals protects refactoring freedom and semantic versioning, not already-built consumers: a bundler inlines whatever it can reach, so anything reachable at runtime is part of the de-facto contract.
